_comment: Every chip this repo documents, and how a person with nothing but the
installed CLI can run it. Read scripts/ci/docs-runnable-chips.sh for the
rules; the short version is that each chip must be in exactly one bucket,
and 'blocked' entries are re-run too so that a fix cannot sit unnoticed.
Firmware comes from the firmware-demos release: prebuilt ELFs, pinned by
tag AND sha256, so nothing here needs a cross toolchain and a re-uploaded
asset cannot silently change what the gate proves.
`expect` is a line the firmware itself prints. It is deliberately not an
exit code: `labwired run` treats a simulation error as a non-fatal end of
run and still exits 0, so exit status alone proves nothing here.

rv1103.why: Optional source-built qemu-arm-system reduced Linux direct boot and joint I2C3/UART4 basket acceptance exist at functional 24MHz; default/released CLI cannot run this board. Vendor BSP/SD/ROM boot, complete RV1103 and physical qualification remain unavailable; this is not an installed CLI command

esp32c6.note: ESP32-C6-DevKitC-1 L1 smoke. Bare-metal RV32IMAC HP-core image ungates UART0 through the C6's own PCR clock/reset block, routes GPIO16/U0TXD via IO_MUX, and prints OK. The LP core, ROM bootloader/flash-image path, interrupt delivery, radios and every non-UART peripheral window are out of scope at L1.

nrf54l15.note: The README quickstart. Firmware is committed, so a clone is enough.

nrf54lm20a.note: Snake on an RM67162 AMOLED over SPIM22. Firmware is committed (tests/fixtures/nrf54lm20a-snake.elf), so a clone plus the CLI is the whole prerequisite. The expected map is read back from the model: each value reaches memory or GPIO3 outside the nRF54L15 sibling's map.

stm32u5a5zj.why: The U5A5 Nucleo model and source UART smoke are in this repository, but the smoke firmware is built from source (examples/nucleo-u5a5zj/io-smoke.yaml); there is no committed ELF or firmware-demos release asset for an installed CLI

atmega1281.note: The 64-pin target uses its AVR-GCC reset image. The CLI smoke asserts the USART0 banner and the PB5 status LED; the Playground uses this same compiled ELF.

atmega2561.note: 64-pin ATmega2561 on the shared public AVR core. The committed tiny ELF prints `2561 OK` through USART0 and drives PB5; the script verdict is asserted because `labwired test` does not echo the AVR console.

atmega2560.note: AVR runs through a system manifest, not `labwired run`, and `labwired test` does not echo the AVR console, so the expectation is the script verdict line: it asserts the USART0 banner and a report line with A8/A9 read through ADCSRB.MUX5.

atmega328p.note: AVR runs through a system manifest, not `labwired run`. Blinky drives a pin and prints nothing, so the assertion is that it executes its whole step budget without faulting.

atsamd21g18a.note: Bare-metal SERCOM0 bring-up for the Arduino Zero / Feather M0 class. Same ELF `cargo build -p firmware-samd21-demo --release` produces from crates/firmware-samd21-demo (build from that directory, not the workspace root: its -Tlink.x comes from its own .cargo/config.toml, and a root build links entry 0x0 and boots nowhere while succeeding). Committed so a clone plus the CLI is the whole prerequisite. The expected line is the SECOND the firmware prints, so a model that sets INTFLAG.DRE once and forgets emits only the first and fails here.
